newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN INSURERS' H1 PREMIUMS SLIP IN REAL TERMS.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN INSURERS' H1 PREMIUMS SLIP IN REAL TERMS.

text.p: Russian insurers' premiums slipped in real terms in the first half of 1997 compared to the same period last year, a finance ministry official said on Thursday.
Valery Sukhov, head of the ministry's insurance supervision department, forecast insurance companies would finish the year flat in inflation-adjusted terms.
Insurers' premiums rose by 12 percent to 15 trillion roubles ($2.58 billion) in the first half of 1997.
"Even if premiums had risen by 50 percent, or doubled, we would have failed to reach a normal insurance level," Sukhov told a news conference. "To reach it, we must have a rise of 20 to 30 times."

The Russian commercial insurance industry which emerged after the start of economic reforms in the early 1990s, is going through difficult times. Insurance has fallen victim to economic stagnation and companies' failure to appreciate the need for commercial insurance.
Sukhov said the number of insurance companies had shrunk by 15 percent to 2,410 in the period from July 1, 1996, to July 1, 1997.
He said the volume of property and liability insurance had risen due to a start of investment in real sector.
